doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Work, pay and the New York life
title: Logistics and pay of corporate gigs in Manhattan
summary: Hauling a PA and bass into midtown, parking, and corporate gigs paying $300 or more.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: In the really small sense though, sometimes I envision you and drummers especially playing a club date in New York and logistically I would think that’s probably a pain sometimes. Like parking your car.

You can say that. I don’t know how many gigs I’ve done in midtown where you really have to call someone. “I need help.” Sometimes I have to take a PA, particularly if they want me to sing and play the whole night. So you’ve got a PA, an acoustic bass and an amplifier and the gig is upstairs at the Crown Plaza on 42nd Street. How do you do this? Except put your hazards on, panic, get help, get your stuff inside, make sure someone is watching it, go and park. It’s a nightmare. But you find a way. The best thing about — you really have to be organized, you know what I mean? I mean the more organization and the more time you give yourself, you know, the better off you will be. And you have to go and do your own research. Sometimes the best parking will be a comp and you can print out a coupon to get cheaper parking somewhere, you know. And you have to know do the streets go this way on that street? You really have to know midtown Manhattan to survive it. Yeah it’s rough. That’s the hardest part. To me it’s not the playing and singing and smiling on those gigs, you know, the corporate gigs. All it is is turn up, play, sing and smile and that doing what the gig requires you know, you’re back in the music. But the other stuff, wow. That’s a challenge.
What does a gig like that pay if you don’t mind my asking.
Um it varies. Well it’s as low as $300 really or even lower. But if I don’t sing or do anything else it could be lower. But maybe $300 to $5, $6 even more. Generally not more these days.
